As silly as it may be, are there certain distros that work really well with laptops? I have Fedora dual booting on my laptop at the moment, and it chews through my batter a lot quicker than windows does. I've tried finding battery monitors, but it doesn't seem to help that much. For example, if I ran Mint, or Debian, would it be able to handle battery consumption better?

There are some quick battery optimizations that you can do with your current distro. I haven't tried this with Fedora 23 yet but so far I haven't had any issues with compatibility for other software on 23. I know some distros are going to be slightly better or worse, but I've figured that Linux just isn't all that well optimized for battery life on laptops.

I have no comparison data, but I feel that my laptop runs for quite a long time on battery. I use Linux Mint 17.2 Cinnamon. One handy feature is that I can dim the screen brightness by rolling the mouse wheel over the battery icon - not intuitive, but really handy.
I prefer mate cause i can disable composition that dramaticaly increase battery life for amd cards

I don't know how its successors do battery wise, but back in the day crunchbang really extended my laptops battery life. Openbox with tint2 is crazy lightweight. https://www.bunsenlabs.org/ is the main successor if you care to try it. (I don't have a laptop anymore, or else I'd try it myself)

KDE lets you configure many battery profiles for when you're running plugged-in, full, medium, low, etc. I'm sure you could use those to conserve battery more aggressively. You can even change the configuration so that even at full battery it tries it's best to conserve power. I'm not sure if Gnome offers something as easy to use.

Remember too that every battery has a life of it's own - it may be that yours just needs replacing but otherwise there is no magic to it - the more CPU you use the less a full battery will last so you can always try removing programs you don't need, desktop effects, use a blank screen saver instead of an animation, etc. Following this logic using any distro built for weak computers will maximize your battery life too.
The best result I've had for battery on laptop is to install some of the lighter weight distros. If you're hell bent on sticking with the major distros, then consider turning off desktop composition.
If you have a way to control your backlight, I've found lowering mine can gain me as much as a half hour. And as others have said, you can try a more lightweight distro.
